analyses.purpose: A thin planning-gate alias. ralplan = `/oh-my-claudecode:plan --consensus`. Two jobs: (1) a PRE-EXECUTION GATE that intercepts underspecified ralph/autopilot/team/ultrawork requests (heuristic: <=15 effective words AND no concrete anchor) and redirects them into planning instead of letting execution modes flail on a vague target; (2) a multi-agent CONSENSUS LOOP (Planner -> Architect -> Critic, iterate to APPROVE) that produces a scoped plan whose final artifact MUST embed an ADR block. It is a planning/scoping skill, not a docs graph engine — it drafts a plan artifact marked `pending approval` and never mutates code without explicit execution approval.
analyses.structure: YAML frontmatter (name, description, argument-hint, level: 4) then prose sections: Usage; Flags (--interactive, --deliberate, --architect codex, --critic codex); Planning/Execution Boundary (pending-approval, no-mutation rule); the numbered consensus workflow (step 0 optional companyContext MCP call -> 1 Planner draft + RALPLAN-DR summary -> 2 optional user gate -> 3 Architect steelman review -> 4 Critic quality eval -> 5 re-review loop max 5 iters on ITERATE/REJECT -> 6 mark pending-approval + emit ADR -> 7/8 optional approval + hand off to Skill(team)/Skill(ralph)); a hard "steps 3 and 4 run sequentially, never parallel-batch" callout; then the Pre-Execution Gate reference (why-it-exists, Good/Bad prompt lists, a concrete-Signal detection table, an end-to-end flow example, a troubleshooting table). Agents/tools it loads on demand: Planner + Architect + Critic subagents (Architect/Critic optionally swapped to Codex CLI), AskUserQuestion, an optional companyContext MCP tool, and downstream Skill(team)/Skill(ralph) for execution. It owns no MCP of its own — all real logic lives in the Plan skill it aliases.
key_steps: Gate check: detect execution keyword + underspecified prompt (<=15 effective words, no file/issue/symbol/test/error/code-block anchor, honoring force:/! escape); redirect to planning if vague

Planner drafts the plan + a compact RALPLAN-DR deliberation summary (Principles 3-5, top-3 Decision Drivers, >=2 Viable Options with bounded pros/cons, invalidation rationale if only one option survives)

Deliberate mode (flag or auto on high-risk signals: auth/security, migrations, destructive changes, PII/compliance, public-API breakage) adds a 3-scenario pre-mortem + expanded unit/integration/e2e/observability test plan
Architect review: strongest steelman antithesis + at least one real tradeoff tension + synthesis; flags principle violations — MUST complete before Critic

Critic evaluation against quality criteria (principle-option consistency, fair alternatives, risk-mitigation clarity, testable acceptance criteria, concrete verification); emits APPROVE / ITERATE / REJECT
Re-review loop: any non-APPROVE verdict re-runs the full Planner->Architect->Critic closed loop, max 5 iterations, else present best version

On APPROVE mark plan `pending approval` and emit a final ADR block (Decision, Drivers, Alternatives considered, Why chosen, Consequences, Follow-ups); execute only on explicit approval via Skill(team)/Skill(ralph)
reuse_points: ADR block schema is already spelled out and directly harvestable: 'Decision, Drivers, Alternatives considered, Why chosen, Consequences, Follow-ups' — seed this as the ADR node's typed field set in governance/corpus/ (it maps 1:1 to node attributes).

RALPLAN-DR deliberation shape (Principles / Decision Drivers / Viable Options+pros-cons / explicit invalidation rationale for rejected alternatives) is a ready-made rationale schema for PRD and RFC/DD nodes, and its 'invalidation rationale' concept is the natural home for conflicts_with edge justification.

The Pre-Execution Gate's signal-detection engine (concrete-anchor table: file path, issue #, camelCase/PascalCase/snake_case symbol, test runner, error ref, code block; word-count heuristic; force:/! escape) is structurally identical to the docs-as-code anchor extractor + ambiguity gate — reuse the pattern as the anchor-extraction / untyped_anchor / anchor_fingerprint_drift detector and as the NEEDS_CLARIFICATION (ambiguity<=0.2) promotion block.

The Planner->Architect->Critic authoring/review SEPARATION (writer drafts, separate reviewer lane evaluates) is the correct shape for graph-node authoring: a writer pass mutates node/edge drafts, a review pass evaluates — matches the repo doctrine 'keep authoring and review as separate passes / never self-approve'.

Planning/Execution Boundary (artifact stays `pending approval`, no mutation before explicit approval) maps directly onto the docs-as-code 'rendered md/json are BUILD ARTIFACTS, commit-only writes' rule — the skill drafts graph deltas and gates the compile/emit step, never hand-edits the rendered outputs.

Deliberate-mode high-risk auto-enable list (auth/security, migrations, destructive, PII, public-API breakage) is reusable as the policy-as-data predicate for WHICH decisions must carry a ratified ADR + clarification node before promotion past accepted (feeds unratified_design / unimplemented_decision / conflicting_accepted_pair invariants).

The Good/Bad-prompt lists, Signal table, and Troubleshooting table are a strong UX template for documenting the deterministic invariant codes (unrealized_requirement, unratified_design, unimplemented_decision, anchor_fingerprint_drift, etc.) as a 'what tripped / how to satisfy it' reference in the new skill body.

Frontmatter template (name / description / argument-hint / level: 4) and the --architect codex / --critic codex cross-model flags — reuse the flag pattern to route the ADVISORY LLM/NLI semantic-contradiction pass to a cross-model reviewer (Codex-xhigh), keeping it advisory.
analyses.amend_vs_seed_signal: Favors SEEDING a fresh /documentation-and-adrs skill and HARVESTING fragments from ralplan — not amending ralplan or absorbing it wholesale. Reasons: (1) Architecture mismatch — ralplan is a stateless consensus PLANNING gate that produces a one-shot plan artifact; the docs-as-code target is a persistent typed relational GRAPH (governance/corpus/) with a deterministic invariant evaluator (extending the existing cross-artifact-agreement evaluator), build-artifact compilation of md/json, anchor extraction, MIF conformance levels, and a stranger-repo fixture gate — none of which ralplan contains or is shaped for. (2) A direct doctrinal CONFLICT: ralplan's core mechanism is 'the Critic LLM verdict gates the loop,' but the target's enforcement bar is 'deterministic graph invariants BLOCK; the LLM/NLI pass is ADVISORY-ONLY, never a merge verdict' (evidence-admissibility bar). Copying ralplan's consensus-verdict-as-gate would violate that bar; the consensus loop can only be reused as the ADVISORY authoring/review lane, never as the blocking gate. (3) ralplan is a SHARED OMC plugin skill used by ralph/autopilot/team routing — amending oyatie's docs-graph semantics into it would corrupt that shared surface and violate the single-source runtime-skill contract. (4) An existing generic agent-skills:documentation-and-adrs already occupies the name but only does generic decision-recording, not the graph model — so it also can't be reused as-is. Net: seed a new neutral-engine + policy-as-data skill; borrow ralplan's ADR/RALPLAN-DR schemas, its gate/signal-detection heuristic (as the clarification/anchor gate), its authoring-vs-review separation, and its frontmatter/flag template; explicitly DO NOT carry over the consensus-loop-as-merge-verdict.

analyses.purpose: A deep, multi-source, fact-checked research harness: takes a research question (via args), and via a fan-out multi-agent pipeline produces a cited, adversarially-verified report. whenToUse tells it to ask 2-3 clarifying questions FIRST if the question is underspecified, then run.
analyses.structure: A compiled JS workflow-script harness (NOT markdown), driven by the native workflow runtime primitives: meta export {name, description, whenToUse, phases[]}; phase(name); agent(prompt,{label,phase,schema}) -> schema-validated structured output; pipeline(items, stage1Fn, stage2Fn) streaming (no barrier between stages); parallel([fn,...]); log(msg). It defines JSON-Schema constants (SCOPE/SEARCH/EXTRACT/VERDICT/REPORT) so every agent boundary returns TYPED structured data, with deterministic plain-JS glue between agents (URL normalize+dedup, relevance/importance/quality ranking, fetch budget, 3-vote quorum adjudication). Five phases: Scope (1 agent decomposes question into 3-6 angles) -> Search (N parallel WebSearch agents) -> Fetch (WebFetch+extract 2-5 falsifiable claims/source, streamed via pipeline with dedup+budget) -> Verify (per-claim 3 parallel adversarial voters; DETERMINISTIC adjudication in JS: survives = valid_votes>=2 AND refutes<2, abstain!=survive, default-refute-if-uncertain) -> Synthesize (1 agent merges semantic dupes, ranks by confidence, cites sources). Every phase has a graceful-degradation/salvage return (no scope->error; no claims->partial; all-refuted->inconclusive; synth-fail->raw claims). Ported from a 'bughunter' fan-out/verify architecture.
key_steps: Scope: one agent decomposes the input (args) into 3-6 complementary typed sub-targets against SCOPE_SCHEMA
Fan-out gather: N parallel agents collect candidate items, each returning schema-validated structured output
Streaming pipeline with dedup+budget: normalize/fingerprint each item (normURL), drop duplicates and over-budget low-relevance items, no barrier between gather and extract
Extract: per-source agent emits 2-5 FALSIFIABLE typed claims each with a supporting quote + importance + source-quality rating (EXTRACT_SCHEMA)
Rank+cap the claim pool deterministically (importance then source-quality), slice to MAX_VERIFY_CLAIMS

Adversarial verify: 3 parallel skeptical voter agents per claim, but ADJUDICATE deterministically in JS (quorum of valid votes AND refutes<REQUIRED; abstentions do NOT pass; default to refuted if uncertain)
Synthesize: one agent merges semantic duplicates, groups into findings, assigns per-finding confidence, writes summary+caveats+openQuestions, cites sources (REPORT_SCHEMA)
Return a structured report with provenance (sources), refuted-claims transparency list, and stats incl. agentCalls; every phase can early-return a salvage/partial result
reuse_points: THE 5-PHASE HARNESS SKELETON as the template for the /documentation-and-adrs workflow script: meta{name,description,whenToUse,phases} + phase()/agent()/pipeline()/parallel()/log(). Map Scope->decompose the doc corpus + ADR frontmatter affected_surfaces.crates into extraction targets; Search/Fetch->run anchor-extractors over ADR/PRD/RFC markdown + code AST to emit TYPED NODES (requirement/design/decision) and declared edges (realized_by/ratified_by/implemented_by/conflicts_with); Verify->run the graph invariants; Synthesize->COMPILE rendered ADR/PRD/RFC md + JSON SSOT out of the graph (the projection).

STRUCTURED-OUTPUT-PER-AGENT WITH JSON SCHEMA (EXTRACT_SCHEMA/VERDICT_SCHEMA): reuse as the typed-node contract enforced at every extraction agent boundary — node schemas (RequirementNode/DesignNode/DecisionNode) + edge schemas — so extraction can't emit an untyped anchor (directly feeds the untyped_anchor invariant).

THE TWO-TIER SPLIT (adversarial LLM votes vs DETERMINISTIC JS adjudication) is the crown-jewel reuse but MUST BE INVERTED for admissibility: in docs-as-code the DETERMINISTIC tier is the ONLY blocker (owned-Rust graph invariants: unrealized_requirement, unratified_design, unimplemented_decision, conflicting_accepted_pair, anchor_fingerprint_drift, untyped_anchor, unresolved_clarification, + status/propagation/supersession codes), and the LLM/NLI semantic-contradiction pass is ADVISORY-ONLY (files an issue, never a merge verdict). deep-research's 'default to refuted if uncertain / abstentions do NOT pass / all-abstain must not false-survive' quorum logic is exactly the evidence-admissibility discipline (BLOCKED=valid grade, no tuned-toward-PASS emulated measurements).

normURL DEDUP + FINGERPRINT + BUDGET pattern -> node identity by stable anchor fingerprint / content-address; this is literally the mechanism behind the anchor_fingerprint_drift invariant and reverse-edge-derived-from-one-declared-end (Backstage trick) so the two ends can't disagree.

whenToUse 'ask 2-3 clarifying questions if underspecified' -> maps 1:1 onto the NEEDS_CLARIFICATION ambiguity node that blocks promotion past accepted (ambiguity<=0.2 doctrine); the unresolved_clarification invariant is the graph realization of deep-research's clarify-before-run gate.

GRACEFUL-DEGRADATION / SALVAGE RETURNS at every phase -> the evaluator must emit a determinate, fail-closed verdict at each stage even when a phase yields nothing (report, don't game; partial verdict carries the blocking codes rather than false-greening).

FINAL REPORT WITH PROVENANCE+STATS (findings/sources/evidence/vote + caveats + openQuestions + stats) -> rendered doc build-artifacts carry source-anchor provenance (citations back to code AST), openQuestions become NEEDS_CLARIFICATION nodes, stats become per-code invariant counts + live md/json before/after count.
analyses.amend_vs_seed_signal: SEED A FRESH /documentation-and-adrs WORKFLOW using deep-research's harness as the STRUCTURAL TEMPLATE — do NOT amend deep-research itself. Three reasons. (1) Not physically amendable: deep-research is a native skill COMPILED INTO the CLI binary; there is no editable SKILL.md source, only a generated per-run .js, so 'amend in place' is not even available. (2) Semantic inversion, not a tweak: deep-research's verification model is 'LLM adversarial vote IS the verdict' (2/3 refutes KILLS a claim). The docs-as-code target REQUIRES the opposite — deterministic graph invariants are the sole BLOCK and the LLM/NLI pass is ADVISORY-ONLY (evidence-admissibility bar). Dragging deep-research's LLM-verdict model in would violate the merge-authority constraint. (3) Different deliverable + different language: the enforcement half must be owned-Rust EXTENDING THE EXISTING cross-artifact-agreement evaluator (no new subsystem, no new python/shell/CLI/deps) — entirely outside deep-research's JS harness. The existing addy agent-skills:documentation-and-adrs is also the wrong base to amend (it teaches writing MORE markdown ADRs; the target compiles md OUT of a graph). NET: reuse is PATTERN-LEVEL — clone deep-research's 5-phase fan-out->extract-typed-nodes->verify->synthesize scaffold, its structured-output-per-agent contract, its dedup/fingerprint/budget glue, its deterministic-adjudication-separate-from-LLM discipline, and its clarify-if-ambiguous + graceful-degradation behaviors — while INVERTING verification to deterministic-BLOCK + LLM-advisory and pointing the enforcement at the owned-Rust evaluator. Ship shape = neutral engine + ontology-pack/rulepack/anchor-extractors as DATA, with the stranger-repo (REQUIREMENT->TEST->MODULE) fixture as a required gate.

design.rationale:
SEED the thin `/documentation-and-adrs` SKILL.md; AMEND the existing owned-Rust corpus + evaluator; do NOT amend deep-research or ralplan (relate to them one-way instead). Three grounded reasons.

(1) The enforcement half is already ~70% built as owned Rust, and the target explicitly says "extend the EXISTING cross-artifact-agreement evaluator, do NOT build a new subsystem." I verified the substrate exists and is the right shape: `cloud/cloud-ci/gates/oya-cloud-ci-cross-artifact-agreement-app/src/lib.rs` is a pure, fixture-driven evaluator whose own docstring already states "carve-outs/exceptions live as DATA, never as evaluator branches" (that IS the neutral-engine + policy-as-data ship shape, already satisfied). It already emits decision-face codes that map 1:1 to the target's "status/propagation/supersession" codes (status_disagreement, unpropagated_decision, supersession_half_edge, dual_decision_collision, phantom_decision_citation). And `governance/corpus/{core,doc-parser,work-area-rust-parser,extract}` already provides: content-addressed anchors (`core::Function::signature_hash`, invariant under body edits = the `anchor_fingerprint_drift` mechanism), ADR/PRD/RFC Markdown→node parsing (`doc-parser`, ADR-0517/ADR-0541 "documents and directives become first-class corpus graph nodes"), Rust-AST→node facts (`work-area-rust-parser` = the `implemented_by` reality), and a projection binary (`extract`). Building fresh via Ouroboros would birth a from-scratch artifact that then has to be reconciled against all of this — net new friction, and the Ouroboros seed MECHANISM (Python/uv/MCP/~/.ouroboros) violates owned-Rust/no-new-python-shell/no-new-deps outright.

(2) The "amend deep-research + ralplan" option is dead on arrival for the two named skills: deep-research is COMPILED INTO the CLI binary (no editable SKILL.md — physically un-amendable), and ralplan is a SHARED OMC plugin skill routed by ralph/autopilot/team — encoding oyatie's docs-graph semantics into it corrupts a shared surface and violates the single-source runtime-skill contract. Their doctrinal core (Critic-LLM-verdict-gates-the-loop) also directly conflicts with the target's merge-authority bar (deterministic invariants BLOCK; LLM is advisory-only). So they are reused at the PATTERN level and connected by a one-way ingestion contract, never edited.

(3) The `/documentation-and-adrs` skill itself does not exist and is cheap to seed — it's a thin orchestrator SKILL.md, not a subsystem. So the honest label is HYBRID: seed one small markdown skill + surgically amend existing owned-Rust crates + relate (not amend) the two upstream skills. Calling it "seed-new-skill" understates the mandated amend of the evaluator/corpus; calling it "amend-deep-research-and-ralplan" is flatly wrong (can't/shouldn't touch those).
design.skill_purpose: `/documentation-and-adrs` is a user-invoked authoring-and-gate orchestrator that turns a PRD/RFC/ADR change into typed graph mutations in `governance/corpus/`, compiles the rendered docs as build artifacts out of the graph, and runs the deterministic cross-artifact invariants as the sole merge authority — with an LLM/NLI contradiction pass that is advisory-only. It does NOT hand-write Markdown ADRs (that is the retired paradigm of the addy `agent-skills:documentation-and-adrs`); it makes contradiction structurally impossible by deriving both the rendered md and the JSON SSOT from one graph whose edges are anchored to code-AST reality, so live md/json count drops and freshness is automatic. The skill owns orchestration + the ambiguity gate + the authoring/review separation; all real enforcement lives in the owned-Rust corpus crates and the cross-artifact-agreement evaluator it drives, keeping the engine neutral and the ontology/rulepack as swappable DATA (proven by a stranger-repo fixture).
skill_steps: 1. INGEST & CLASSIFY. Read the change surface: the ADR/PRD/RFC blocks authored in the branch, plus any handed-in deep-research REPORT or ralplan ADR-block artifacts. Classify each block into exactly one node type (requirement / design / decision / clarification). Anything that maps to no type is refused up front (pre-check for untyped_anchor) — no free-form prose enters the graph.

2. AUTHOR AS GRAPH MUTATION. Express each doc as a typed node DRAFT satisfying the node contract (id, type, status, anchors[], rationale fields, edges), written into governance/corpus/ via the doc-parser node layer. Declare each traceability edge from ONE end only: realized_by on the requirement, ratified_by on the design, implemented_by sourced from the ADR frontmatter affected_surfaces.crates, conflicts_with (symmetric, carrying an invalidation-rationale note). Reverse edges (realizes/ratifies/implements) are DERIVED by the engine and never hand-authored — the Backstage trick, so the two ends cannot disagree.

3. ANCHOR-BIND to code-AST reality (Foundry projection). For every implemented_by edge, resolve the target crate/fn to a corpus content-address (core::Function::signature_hash). The node pins to the live signature, not to prose. An implemented_by whose target resolves to no live corpus fact is dangling; an anchor the extractor cannot type is untyped_anchor. Because signature_hash is invariant under body edits but churns on rename/removal/visibility change, later code drift trips anchor_fingerprint_drift automatically — freshness is a property of content-addressing, not a manual sync step.

4. AMBIGUITY GATE (deterministic, blocking). Score residual ambiguity with a DETERMINISTIC structural predicate (requirement has >=1 testable acceptance-criterion anchor AND a realized_by target; borrowed from ralplan's concrete-anchor signal table) — never an LLM judgment, since only deterministic evidence may block. If ambiguity > 0.2, emit a NEEDS_CLARIFICATION node that blocks promotion past `accepted` (unresolved_clarification). Ask the founder the focused questions via AskUserQuestion, fold answers into node fields, re-score to <=0.2. This is the deep-interview/Ouroboros ambiguity<=0.2 doctrine realized as a graph node.

5. COMPILE docs as build artifacts. Run the corpus render mode (extend governance/corpus/extract) to project the graph into rendered ADR/PRD/RFC Markdown + the JSON SSOT. The skill NEVER hand-edits these rendered faces — they are commit-only generated outputs governed by the generated-artifact-decommit doctrine. Because both faces derive from one graph, they cannot contradict each other, and consolidating hand-maintained md/json into generated faces drops the live count.

6. RUN DETERMINISTIC INVARIANTS (sole merge authority). Invoke the extended oya-cloud-ci-cross-artifact-agreement evaluator on the graph projection. It returns {verdict, violations} over the blocking codes: the seven new ones (unrealized_requirement, unratified_design, unimplemented_decision, conflicting_accepted_pair, anchor_fingerprint_drift, untyped_anchor, unresolved_clarification) plus the eight already-shipped decision-face codes (status/propagation/supersession). RED blocks; per-(code,key) ratchet baseline handles pre-existing debt. This verdict is the only merge gate.

7. LLM/NLI ADVISORY PASS (never a verdict). Run a semantic-contradiction reviewer (optionally cross-model via --advisor codex, reusing ralplan's --architect/--critic codex flag pattern) over node bodies to catch contradictions the structural codes cannot see (e.g. two Accepted decisions that semantically clash without a declared conflicts_with edge). It FILES AN ISSUE / surfaces candidates only — it cannot change the evaluator verdict. Evidence-admissibility bar: no tuned-toward-PASS emulated measurement is ever admitted as merge authority.

8. SEPARATE REVIEW LANE. The authoring pass (this skill) drafts node/edge mutations marked pending-approval; a distinct reviewer/verifier lane evaluates in a fresh context — never self-approve in the same lane. Promotion evidence = green deterministic gate + the advisory issue (resolved or accepted-as-noise) + reviewer APPROVE.

9. STRANGER-REPO CONFORMANCE (required gate). The same neutral engine, run with a swapped ontology-pack (REQUIREMENT->TEST->MODULE, a non-ADR repo), must pass its fixture gate. This proves the engine carries zero repo-specific logic and that the ADR/PRD/RFC ontology + rulepack are pure DATA, satisfying the portability constraint.
design.node_and_edge_authoring:
NODE CONTRACT (typed node, authored into governance/corpus via doc-parser, ADR-0541 direction). Every node carries: id (PRD-NNNN / DD-NNNN / ADR-NNNN); type in {requirement, design, decision, clarification}; status in {proposed, accepted, superseded, ...}; anchors[] (content-address bindings to corpus core::Function::signature_hash — the code-AST reality); rationale fields harvested straight from ralplan's ADR block + RALPLAN-DR schema (decision, drivers, alternatives_considered, why_chosen, invalidation_rationale, consequences, follow_ups); and edges declared from this node's end only. A node with no type, or an anchor the extractor cannot type, is untyped_anchor and is refused before it reaches the graph.

TRACEABILITY EDGES (declared once, reverse derived — the Backstage trick). realized_by: requirement -> design, declared on the requirement (reverse `realizes` derived). ratified_by: design -> decision, declared on the design (reverse `ratifies` derived). implemented_by: decision -> crate/fn anchors, NOT hand-authored — sourced from the ADR frontmatter affected_surfaces.crates and joined to work-area-rust-parser facts (reverse `implements` derived from the live Rust AST). conflicts_with: decision <-> decision, symmetric, carrying the invalidation_rationale as its justification. Because each edge is stored on exactly one end and the engine materializes the reverse, the two ends can never disagree — the class of half-edge bug the evaluator already names supersession_half_edge is eliminated by construction for the new edge types.

PROJECTION (Foundry) makes freshness automatic: implemented_by resolves through core::Function::signature_hash, which is invariant under body edits and pure reformatting but churns on rename/removal/visibility change. So when code moves out from under a decision, anchor_fingerprint_drift fires on the next evaluation with no manual re-linking. Rendered ADR/PRD/RFC md + JSON SSOT are compiled OUT of this graph (extract render mode), so they are build artifacts, not authored sources — contradiction between the two faces is structurally impossible and reduces to the existing generated_face_drift code if a face is ever stale.

INVARIANT MAP (extend, don't rebuild). New blocking codes added to the evaluator's VIOLATION_CODES + evaluate_keyed(): unrealized_requirement (requirement with no realized_by to an accepted design), unratified_design (design with no ratified_by to an accepted decision), unimplemented_decision (Accepted decision whose implemented_by anchors resolve to no live corpus fact — the requirement/design-aware generalization of the existing orphan_decision/unpropagated_decision), conflicting_accepted_pair (two Accepted decisions joined by conflicts_with — extends the status/supersession logic already present), anchor_fingerprint_drift (recorded anchor hash != live core signature_hash), untyped_anchor, unresolved_clarification (NEEDS_CLARIFICATION node with ambiguity > 0.2 on a node promoted past accepted). The eight existing decision-face codes are reused verbatim as the "status/propagation/supersession" family. Every code keeps the existing Finding{code,key} keyed shape so the per-(code,key) going-live ratchet baselines pre-existing debt exactly as today.
design.relation_to_deep_research: One-way typed INGESTION, never an amendment (deep-research is compiled into the CLI binary and cannot be edited anyway). deep-research already emits schema-validated structured output — a REPORT with findings (each with confidence + source provenance), a refuted-claims transparency list, and openQuestions. `/documentation-and-adrs` consumes that REPORT as an input artifact and maps it into the graph: each verified finding with a testable claim becomes a candidate requirement node (status=proposed, anchors pulled from the finding's cited sources/code refs); each openQuestion becomes a NEEDS_CLARIFICATION node (deep-research's own whenToUse 'ask 2-3 clarifying questions if underspecified' is the same ambiguity<=0.2 gate, now persisted as a graph node instead of a transient prompt). deep-research's crown discipline — deterministic JS adjudication separate from the adversarial LLM votes, with 'default to refuted if uncertain / abstentions do NOT pass' — is the exact evidence-admissibility posture we keep, but INVERTED for merge authority: in docs-as-code the deterministic Rust invariants are the only blocker and the LLM contradiction pass is advisory. So research flows research -> requirement/clarification nodes, and the harvest is pattern-level (the 5-phase fan-out->extract-typed-output->verify->synthesize skeleton informs the skill's ingest/classify/anchor/render shape) with zero edits to deep-research itself.
design.relation_to_ralplan: One-way INGESTION + schema harvest, never an amendment (ralplan is a shared OMC plugin routed by ralph/autopilot/team; editing it would corrupt that shared surface and its Critic-LLM-verdict-gates-the-loop core conflicts with our deterministic-only merge bar). ralplan already ends every consensus plan with a fully specified ADR block (Decision, Drivers, Alternatives considered, Why chosen, Consequences, Follow-ups) plus a RALPLAN-DR deliberation summary (Principles, Decision Drivers, Viable Options + bounded pros/cons, explicit invalidation rationale for rejected options). `/documentation-and-adrs` ingests that ADR block/plan artifact and maps it to a decision node whose rationale fields ARE ralplan's ADR-block fields 1:1, with the RALPLAN-DR invalidation-rationale becoming the justification carried on any conflicts_with edge, and the plan's design content becoming a design (DD-NNNN) node linked ratified_by -> the decision. ralplan's pending-approval / no-mutation boundary maps onto our commit-only build-artifact rule (the skill drafts graph deltas and gates the compile step, never hand-edits rendered outputs); its Planner->Architect->Critic authoring-vs-review SEPARATION is reused as the writer-drafts / separate-reviewer-lane discipline; its pre-execution concrete-anchor signal table is reused as the deterministic ambiguity-gate predicate. Explicitly NOT carried over: ralplan's consensus-verdict-as-gate — the Critic's APPROVE/ITERATE/REJECT can only feed the ADVISORY lane, never the merge verdict. So planning flows plan -> decision/design (ADR/RFC) nodes, harvesting schema + separation + gate-heuristic while leaving ralplan untouched.
design.deliverable_outline:
TWO parts: (A) a thin SEEDED skill, (B) surgical AMEND diffs to existing owned-Rust surfaces. No new subsystem, no new deps, no python/shell/CLI.

A. SEED — `.omc/skills/documentation-and-adrs/SKILL.md` (project-scoped committable per the worktree doctrine's `.omc/skills/**` exception; namespaced to avoid the addy `agent-skills:documentation-and-adrs` collision).
  - Frontmatter: name, description, argument-hint, level:4, flags: --advisor codex (route the advisory NLI pass cross-model, ralplan pattern), --render-only, --gate-only.
  - Body sections: Purpose; Node contract + edge grammar reference; the 9-step workflow (above); the deterministic-vs-advisory boundary callout (steps 6/7 run sequentially, advisory NEVER changes verdict); an ingestion appendix (deep-research REPORT -> requirement/clarification; ralplan ADR block + RALPLAN-DR -> decision/design); a 'what tripped / how to satisfy it' table for every invariant code (reusing ralplan's Good/Bad + troubleshooting-table UX); the stranger-repo conformance note.
  - Loads on demand: AskUserQuestion (ambiguity gate), the corpus extract binary (render), the evaluator (gate), an optional cross-model advisor. Owns no MCP.

B. AMEND — surgical, per existing file:
  1. governance/corpus/core/src/lib.rs (currently ItemKind = Function/Type/Impl/Route/PubItem for CODE facts): add a sibling typed DOC-node model (requirement/design/decision/clarification) OR — preferred, lower-risk — add the doc-node kinds in the doc-parser layer (ADR-0541 already scopes 'documents/directives as first-class corpus nodes') and keep core as the code-fact + signature_hash anchor source that implemented_by resolves against. Reuse Function::signature_hash unchanged as the anchor identity.
  2. governance/corpus/doc-parser/src/lib.rs: extend the Markdown parser to emit typed PRD/RFC/ADR nodes with the node contract fields + frontmatter edges (realized_by / ratified_by / conflicts_with declared from one end; implemented_by read from affected_surfaces.crates). Add adversarial fixtures for malformed/obfuscated edge targets (the crate's own docstring flags this as a required hardening before any merge-blocking doc invariant consumes its nodes).
  3. governance/corpus/extract/src/main.rs: add a RENDER mode that projects the graph -> rendered ADR/PRD/RFC md + JSON SSOT (compile-out; commit-only faces). Add reverse-edge DERIVATION so only one declared end is authored.
  4. cloud/cloud-ci/gates/oya-cloud-ci-cross-artifact-agreement-app/src/lib.rs: extend VIOLATION_CODES from the current 8 to add unrealized_requirement, unratified_design, unimplemented_decision, conflicting_accepted_pair, anchor_fingerprint_drift, untyped_anchor, unresolved_clarification; extend the fixture Value shape to carry requirement/design nodes + typed edges + per-anchor recorded_hash vs live_hash; add the corresponding branches to evaluate_keyed() with Finding{code,key}. Keep the pure/fixture-driven/carve-outs-as-DATA contract (no scanner special-cases) intact.
  5. specs/fixtures/cross-artifact-agreement/: add tc-XA-good/bad-* fixtures for each new code (e.g. tc-XA-bad-unrealized-requirement, tc-XA-bad-anchor-drift, tc-XA-good-req-design-decision-chain), mirroring the existing frozen-live-exhibit style.
  6. specs/ontology-packs/ (new DATA dir, not code): the ADR/PRD/RFC ontology-pack + rulepack + anchor-extractor config + MIF-conformance-levels as JSON DATA the neutral engine consumes; PLUS a stranger-repo pack (REQUIREMENT->TEST->MODULE, non-ADR) with its own required fixture set — the portability gate.
  7. Governance wiring: land the enabling ADRs Proposed with ratified positions (per the 'land ADRs Proposed, formal Accepted rides propagation' rule), anchored to the existing ADR-0517/0541/0580 corpus cluster; the render step de-commits the newly generated md faces per the generated-artifact-decommit doctrine so live md/json count measurably drops (countable before/after at evaluation).
open_questions: Node home: do requirement/design/decision nodes live as new corpus/core kinds, or as doc-parser typed doc-nodes joined to core (ADR-0541 direction)? Recommendation leans doc-parser to keep core as the pure code-fact + signature_hash anchor source, but founder should ratify the boundary.

Gate ownership: the existing cross-artifact-agreement evaluator is decision/ADR-scoped today. Extending it to span requirement/design invariants is what the target mandates ('extend the existing evaluator'), but is a cross-type PRD/RFC concern better as a sibling gate reusing the same pure engine, so the ADR gate stays single-concern (ADR-0132 no-grouping)? Needs a call.
id/registry authority for the new node types: ADR-NNNN numbering exists; who mints and dedups PRD-NNNN / DD-NNNN, and does dual_decision_collision generalize to dual_requirement/dual_design?

Deterministic ambiguity score definition: the blocking score MUST be a structural predicate (anchor-presence + testable-acceptance-criterion presence), not an LLM judgment. Founder should confirm the exact structural rubric so the <=0.2 threshold is reproducible and admissible.

Live-count reduction accounting: the 'md/json count drops' claim only holds if the rendered faces are DE-COMMITTED (generated-artifact-decommit doctrine), not committed alongside the graph. Confirm rendered ADR/PRD/RFC faces are generated + gitignored/de-committed, and measure before/after at evaluation.

Skill namespace + name collision: the addy `agent-skills:documentation-and-adrs` already occupies the bare name with the opposite (write-more-markdown) paradigm. Confirm the oya-scoped `.omc/skills/documentation-and-adrs/` home and how `/documentation-and-adrs` disambiguates at invocation.

Advisory LLM/NLI pass substrate: reuse a cross-model reviewer (Codex-xhigh) per the --advisor flag, or an owned NLI kernel? Advisory-only either way, but the founder may prefer the owned-stack path long-term.
